newsitem.title: TURKEY: Goodyear sees higher 1997 Turkish sales.
newsitem.headline: Goodyear sees higher 1997 Turkish sales.

text.p: Turkey's leading tire-maker Goodyear Lastikleri A S., a subsidary of Goodyear Tire and Rubber Company, aims to increase its net sales by 5.7 percent in 1997 to $286.5 million despite an unexpected contraction in demand in the first quarter, a senior official said.

"We aim to grow by 5.7 percent on constant dollar basis in 1997. If we had more capacity, perhaps we could grow faster," William Stokel, chairman and managing director of the company, told Reuters in an interview.
The first quarter of 1997 had been "a disapointment" for the company, according to Stokel.

"Unit volume has been noticably down relative to 1996. And frankly, I have no good reason that I can give, why this should be," Stokel said. "There was a noticeable drop in demand relative to first quarter of 1996."
"1996 financially was the second best year in our history on constant dollar basis and operating income was about $46 million, before tax," he said.
Stokel said the company had achieved records both in output and in efficiency last year.
"So we have to very seriously study how to expand the capacity. Because now we are very very close to 100 percent capacity utilisation," he said.
He said Goodyear was trying to overcome capacity problem through capacity expansion investments.
"Significant capacity expansions will have to be achieved with great amount of effort, money and we are prepared to do that, but that does not happen overnight," he added.
The company has a 40 percent share in the local market with two different brands -- Goodyear and Fulda.
Goodyear reported 26.8 trillion lira total sales in 1996 against 15.4 trillion in 1995 and net profit rose to 3.7 trillion from 1.8 trillion.
